title: He helped build Alexa. Now Rohit Prasad is taking over Boston Dynamics
source_used: Manufacturing Dive and Boston Dynamics' own announcement (Fast Company, the item's outlet, returned HTTP 403)
key_facts: Boston Dynamics, owned by Hyundai, announced on 6 Oct 2026 that Rohit Prasad is its new CEO, effective 7 Oct 2026.
Prasad spent 12 years at Amazon, latest as senior vice president and head scientist for Alexa and artificial general intelligence, and led the Amazon Nova model family.
He spent nearly 14 years before that at Raytheon BBN Technologies.
He is expected to join the board once approval is complete.
Former CEO Robert Playter stepped down in February after six years; CFO Amanda McMaster was interim CEO.
Semafor reported in May that senior executives and engineers left after Playter; former employees said they were pressed to put tens of thousands of humanoids into Hyundai plants.
Hyundai plans to deploy 25,000 Atlas units across Kia factories and other global plants, starting in 2028.
quote_evidence: Boston Dynamics, a humanoid and industrial robot maker owned by Hyundai, said it has appointed Rohit Prasad as CEO, effective today.
Hyundai plans to deploy 25,000 Atlas units across its Kia factories and other global plants, with an initial rollout in 2028.
Prasad is expected to join Boston Dynamics’ board of directors as soon as the approval process is completed, a spokesperson confirmed via email Wednesday.
why_it_matters_hint: A leader from consumer AI takes over a company whose humanoid robots are about to be tested in car factories.
notes: Fast Company profile (8 Oct) not readable; facts from Manufacturing Dive and the company release. Older news re-dated: appointment was announced 6 Oct.
